title: Free Printable Dinosaur Bingo Cards for Class and Parties
metaDescription: Free printable dinosaur bingo with 36 prehistoric names, from Tyrannosaurus to Stegosaurus, plus fossils and eras. Print for school units or a dino party.
intro: Print free dinosaur bingo cards with 36 real prehistoric animals and fossil terms. They suit a science unit, a party or a rainy day with a pile of dinosaur books.
itemsNote: Real species, three eras and a few science words make this list useful as vocabulary. Some flying and swimming reptiles are included, though strictly they are not dinosaurs, so mention that to older students.

sections.heading: How to play dinosaur bingo
body: Dinosaur names are long and tricky, so this game gives children a reason to practice them. Take it slowly and let the caller say each name syllable by syllable.

1. Give every player a card and a stack of paper bones or small brown counters.
2. The caller reads a name or a clue, for example three horns and a frill, and waits for players to find it.
3. Players say the name together before covering the square.
4. The first player to cover a row or the four corners calls out dig it.
5. Play several rounds and let the winner choose the next caller.

sections.heading: Three prehistoric variations
body:
* **Era sorting.** Before the game, sort the animals into Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous groups. Call only one era each round.
* **Diet bingo.** Players cover only herbivores in the first game, then only carnivores in the second.
* **Fossil hunt.** Bury plastic bones or cardboard cutouts in a sandbox and cover a square for each one that is dug up.

sections.heading: Tips for classroom use
body: Add a pronunciation guide to the board. Many children get stuck on names like Pachycephalosaurus, so a chart with sound-outs takes the pressure off.
Connect the game to what scientists really know. Some dinosaurs had feathers, and birds are their living relatives. A quick mention keeps the lesson current.
Let strong readers act as callers and quiet children as checkers, so every child has a job.

sections.heading: Printing for dino fans
body: Print on sand-colored or green paper and cut the cards to a handy size. Cardstock suits fossils-and-sandbox play because it survives dusty hands.
If you are printing for a party, put a dinosaur name tag on each card as a small favor. Ink saver keeps long names legible without heavy grids.

faq.q: Are all the animals on the list actually dinosaurs?
faq.a: Most are. Pteranodon, Ichthyosaur, Plesiosaur and Mosasaurus were flying or swimming reptiles that lived alongside dinosaurs, which makes a good discussion point.

faq.q: How do children pronounce the names?
faq.a: Break each into syllables, for example tie-RAN-oh-SAW-rus, and say it with them a few times before play starts.
Ages five and up enjoy it. Younger dinosaur fans can play with a 3x3 grid and a grown-up reading the names.
